subject: Post-demo: traffic profile, budget range & recommended service split
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finlytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: traffic profile, budget range & recommended service split

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on the product goals. Quick recap + one ask so we can lock a pilot config and a pricing band for procurement: 

Recap (TL;DR)
- Goal: add generative summaries + semantic search to the analytics workflow; rerank for top-10 result precision on flagship reports.
- Desired SLA: sub-500ms median in US region for customer-facing summaries.

Asks (one slot to fill)
- Can you confirm projected monthly traffic for the pilot (or best estimate): MAUs, average sessions per MAU, average requests that will hit the generation endpoint vs embeddings vs rerank?
- Average tokens per generation request (prompt + expected completion). If you don’t have precise numbers, a best-guess range is fine (e.g., 800–1,400 tokens).
- Target pilot budget range (monthly) you’re comfortable with. This helps us propose options that balance latency vs unit cost (hosted vs dedicated).
- Any hard constraint for $/1M tokens target for the pilot? (we’ve seen customers aim anywhere from $300–$1,200 depending on model mix and SLAs)

I attached a short pricing scenarios sheet (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx) with three illustrative bands — Starter, Scale, Dedicated — and a simple per-model token cost table. If you send a quick traffic profile, I’ll fill the sheet with estimated spend and recommended model routing (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) and a suggested fallback plan.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up Wednesday to review the filled scenario and pick a pilot config. Are you available Wed 9–11 PT?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0183

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: traffic profile, budget range & recommended service split

Ben — thanks for the clear note. Below are the estimates from our product team. Numbers are intentionally conservative for pilot planning.

High-level pilot assumption (30-day pilot)
- User base: 150k MAUs (we’ll sample top 5k active users for feature rollout).
- Average sessions per MAU (per month): 2.
- Generation requests: ~60k generation requests/day -> ~1.8M gen requests/month.
- Avg tokens per generation request: 1,200 tokens (prompt ~300 + completion ~900). -> ~2.16B gen tokens/month.
- Embeddings: batch jobs + on-demand: ~80k embeddings/day -> ~2.4M embeddings/month. Avg tokens per embedding: 512 -> ~1.23B embedding tokens/month.
- Rerank: ~5% of generation flows (~90k rerank ops/month). Rerank tokens are small per op (~150 tokens context) -> ~13.5M rerank tokens/month.

Budget range (monthly) for pilot: $18,000 — $32,000. Procurement prefers a per-month cap rather than a flat commitment to start.

Target unit economics: procurement asked if we can hit <= $900 per 1M tokens as a blended target for pilot (they understand it depends on model choices).

Notes / constraints
- Latency is most important for generation; embeddings can be batched and are more tolerant.
- We’d prefer routing: cheaper model for exploratory summaries, higher-capacity for final customer-facing summaries.

If you can sketch scenarios for the attached workbook, that’ll make procurement conversations easier. Wed 10:00 PT works for us if that’s still open.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Product, FinLytics
priya.shah@finlytics.com

[Inline: quoted earlier pricing sheet placeholder]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finlytics.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: traffic profile, budget range & recommended service split

Priya — really helpful, thanks. I filled the attached MAA draft and the pricing scenarios (attached) with three concrete options using your numbers. Summary below (blended cost per 1M tokens rounded):

Scenario A — Hosted Starter (lowest latency tradeoffs)
- Chat (high-quality model): route 60% of gen tokens to rwd-chat-xl -> $1,100 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings (dense-512): $420 / 1M tokens
- Rerank (light rerank model): $210 / 1M tokens
- Blended: ~ $900 / 1M tokens (just under your target at the higher end of the range)

Scenario B — Hosted Scale (cost-balanced)
- Chat: 40% rwd-chat-xl, 60% rwd-chat-moderate -> blended chat cost drops to $760 / 1M
- Embeddings: $300 / 1M (batching assumed)
- Rerank: $180 / 1M
- Blended: ~ $580 / 1M -> est monthly spend ~$21k on your traffic profile (within $18k–$32k)

Scenario C — Dedicated reservation (best unit economics at commit)
- Chat: multi-variant routing on dedicated pool -> $420 / 1M
- Embeddings: $160 / 1M
- Rerank: $90 / 1M
- Blended: ~ $300 / 1M -> requires a monthly commit and ~2–3 week lead for capacity provisioning

Notes and rationale
- The biggest lever is chat model selection + routing policies. If you accept a small quality delta on exploratory summaries (~30% of gen tokens), option B gives the best direction without a commitment.
- Embeddings savings assume batch windowing (we can batch nightly jobs into the cheaper path).
- Rerank is low volume but can be offloaded to a cheaper CPU path for non-latency-critical flows.

Next steps
1) I attached the MAA-draft.pdf and the redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx with the numbers filled per your profile. Please review the scenarios.
2) If Scenario B looks good, we can push a 30-day pilot clause into procurement and set an upper cap at $32k/month to match your limit; we’ll instrument token-level tracing so you see per-model spend in real time.
3) If you want Dedicated economics, I’ll loop infra and ops to scope capacity and lead times.

Are we still good for Wed 10:00 PT? I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Ben
Attachments: MAA-draft.pdf (PDF, 92KB); redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, updated)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: traffic profile, budget range & recommended service split

Looping you both in — Priya sent the traffic profile and a procurement target (<= $900 / 1M blended). I sketched three scenarios and proposed B as the low-friction pilot (stays within their $18–32k band at our hosted scale mix).

Quick asks from product/commercial side:
- Marissa: can we soften pilot terms to accept a $32k hard cap for month 1, then recontract if they want to continue? Proc is pushing for month-to-month initially.
- Karthik: can your team validate the feasibility of the suggested routing policy (40/60 chat split with automatic fallback) for a 30-day pilot on hosted infra? If we need to reserve a small dedicated pool to hit latency SLOs for top-10 customers, flag lead times and min commit.

Quoted below is Priya’s message for context.
